title: S: Prove inbound payment wording stays evidence only
public_pr_body:
Feed three fake customer replies (“paid”, “remittance” and “payment sent”) through #233's actual delegated inbox ingestion and company-bound recording helpers. Require success, the exact stored email evidence and GET-only mailbox access. Assert every frozen invoice field, unpaid status/amount and empty payment list remain unchanged; any table-write or unexpected RPC fails the test.

Also inspect the actual recording SQL contract so the mock cannot hide a financial write inside mailbox_record_inbound: it stores inbound email and the existing intake RFQ only, never invoices/payments/payment claims.

Assumption: #233 has no dedicated inbound chase/payment-claim classifier. This regression exercises its existing inbox path; it does not invent or claim a classifier. Existing RFQ intake remains unchanged. “Only evidence” here means no financial/payment mutation, not removal of existing mailbox cursor/RFQ bookkeeping. No production code or SQL changed/applied.

Validation: 84 unit tests passed across the new four cases, mailbox-delegated and chase-approve; typecheck and targeted lint passed. DB/runtime proof of the recording procedure and browser/provider checks not run. Draft into #233's codex2/j-chasing-combined-main; no main feature pull, deployment, merge or Ready label.
